title: "flaviLib 150x150 — input/output distribution (v1, 261021)"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true

---

The flaviLib counterpart of viromelib's `fig1A_v7_4panel`. Four panels on one shared taxonomic axis:
what went into the library, what came out as stall sites, which CMs matched, and how long the features are.

**The axis is genus, not family.** flaviLib has only three families — Flaviviridae 270, Hepaciviridae 97,
Pestiviridae 44, plus 28 accessions with no family rank — so a family axis is four bars and carries no
information. Genus is assigned for 294 of 439 accessions; the remaining 145 have a `lowest_group` from the
taxonomy table, which is used as a **fallback** and marked, so nothing is dropped and nothing is silently
promoted to a rank it does not hold.

```
genus_display = genus                         where NCBI assigns one
              = "<lowest_group> (unranked)"   where it does not but a lowest_group exists
              = "(unclassified)"              otherwise
```

**Both Mg2+ conditions are shown together.** 10 mM and 1 mM were called separately and are not replicates
of each other, so the output panels draw them as paired bars rather than pooling them. The input panel has
no condition — it is the library.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(cowplot)
library(svglite)
library(glue)
```

## Paths

```{r paths}
# Copy from the cluster into IN_DIR:
#   data/virus_taxonomy_flaviLib_261021.csv
#   work/07_postproc/261021_flaviLib_150x150/<COND>/261021_flaviLib_150x150_<COND>.sites.csv
# This notebook lives in BASE; inputs are shared with the rank-plot notebook, and each knit writes
# to its own dated, strategy-named folder under plots/ so successive strategies sit side by side
# instead of overwriting one another.
BASE    <- "~/Desktop/viromelib/flaviLib/figures/input_distribution"
# Was figures/fig1_input_dist_rank_plot/, which held TWO figures (this one and the other
# of the pair) -- the reason "input_dist" appeared in two directory names meaning
# different things. Split 2026-10-26, one figure per directory. inputs/ is shared
# between the two and was COPIED into each, with figure_inputs.md5 kept in both so any
# later drift between the copies is detectable.
IN_DIR  <- file.path(BASE, "inputs")
STRATEGY <- "20261021_inputdist_genus_axis_fallback"
OUT_DIR <- file.path(BASE, "plots", STRATEGY)
dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

DS         <- "261021_flaviLib_150x150"
CONDITIONS <- c("10mM", "01mM")
COND_LABEL <- c("10mM" = "10 mM", "01mM" = "1 mM")
COND_COL   <- c("10 mM" = "#3A0CA3", "1 mM" = "#9D8DF1")

TAX_CSV <- file.path(IN_DIR, "virus_taxonomy_flaviLib_261021.csv")

MIN_GENUS_N <- 1      # genera with fewer library accessions than this are pooled into "Other"
FIG_W <- 13; FIG_H <- 7.5
```

## Taxonomy, and the genus axis

```{r taxonomy}
tax <- read_csv(TAX_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    genus_display = case_when(
      !is.na(genus) & genus != ""                 ~ genus,
      !is.na(lowest_group) & lowest_group != ""   ~ paste0(lowest_group, " (unranked)"),
      TRUE                                        ~ "(unclassified)"),
    family_display = ifelse(is.na(family) | family == "", "(no family assigned)", family),
    # feature length from the feature name: ACC|start-end_region
    feat_len = NA_real_)

message(glue("taxonomy: {nrow(tax)} accessions | {n_distinct(tax$taxid)} TaxIDs | ",
             "{sum(!is.na(tax$genus))} with a genus | ",
             "{sum(is.na(tax$genus) & !is.na(tax$lowest_group))} using the lowest_group fallback | ",
             "{n_distinct(tax$genus_display)} axis levels"))

knitr::kable(tax %>% count(family_display, sort = TRUE), caption = "Accessions by family")
knitr::kable(tax %>% count(genus_display, sort = TRUE) %>% head(25),
             caption = "Accessions by genus (with fallback), top 25")
```

## Sites, both conditions

```{r sites}
CM_COLS <- c(
  class1a   = "CL_Class_1a_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
  class1b   = "CL_Class_1b_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
  class1c   = "class1c.cm_hit",
  class2    = "CL_Class_2_xrRNA_final.cm_hit",
  class3    = "cl3_NAR_2025.align.mpkadded.edited.confident.dedup.IDcurated.SS_cons.cm_hit",
  class4    = "class4_cl4_v9_20260824.cm_hit",
  dumbbell  = "dumbbell_RF00525.cm_hit"
)
cm_colors <- c(class1a = "#B5179E", class1b = "#7209B7", class1c = "#C3A1E8",
               class2 = "#3A0CA3", class3 = "#1B998B", class4 = "#136F63",
               dumbbell = "#E9A23B", no_hit = "#CCCCCC")
# viromelib's panel 4 colours 3'UTR orange and intergenic blue. flaviLib has no intergenic
# features, but it does split into annotated vs inferred 3'UTRs, which is the equivalent
# distinction and is worth showing with the same idiom.
region_colors <- c("annotated 3'UTR" = "#E8871A", "inferred 3'UTR" = "#3A7CA5", "other" = "#999999")

cm_labels <- c(class1a = "Class 1a", class1b = "Class 1b", class1c = "Class 1c",
               class2 = "Class 2", class3 = "Class 3", class4 = "Class 4",
               dumbbell = "Dumbbell", no_hit = "No hit")

read_sites <- function(cond) {
  f <- file.path(IN_DIR, glue("{DS}_{cond}.sites.csv"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) stop(glue("missing: {f}"))
  d <- read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  if (!"plain_accession" %in% names(d))
    d <- d %>% mutate(plain_accession = str_extract(accession, "^[^|]+"))
  # CM by lowest E-value, as in the rank plot
  ev <- sapply(names(CM_COLS), function(k) {
    col <- CM_COLS[[k]]
    if (col %in% names(d)) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(d[[col]])))
    else rep(NA_real_, nrow(d))
  })
  ev <- matrix(ev, nrow = nrow(d), dimnames = list(NULL, names(CM_COLS)))
  d$cm_class <- apply(ev, 1, function(r)
    if (all(is.na(r))) "no_hit" else names(r)[which.min(r)])
  d$cm_class <- replace_na(d$cm_class, "no_hit")   # never NA: an NA level adds a stray legend key
  # feature extent, from the feature name: ACC|start-end_region
  d %>% mutate(condition = COND_LABEL[[cond]],
               feat_start = as.numeric(str_match(accession, "\\|(\\d+)-(\\d+)")[, 2]),
               feat_end   = as.numeric(str_match(accession, "\\|(\\d+)-(\\d+)")[, 3]),
               feat_len   = feat_end - feat_start + 1,
               # region, from the tail of the feature name: "_3UTR" vs "_inferred_3UTR"
               region_raw = replace_na(str_match(accession, "\\d+-\\d+_(.+)$")[, 2], ""),
               region     = case_when(str_detect(region_raw, "inferred") ~ "inferred 3'UTR",
                                      str_detect(region_raw, "3UTR")     ~ "annotated 3'UTR",
                                      TRUE ~ "other"))
}

sites <- bind_rows(lapply(CONDITIONS, read_sites)) %>%
  left_join(tax %>% select(plain_accession = accession, genus_display, family_display),
            by = "plain_accession") %>%
  mutate(genus_display = replace_na(genus_display, "(unclassified)"),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = unname(COND_LABEL)),
         cm_class  = factor(cm_class, levels = names(cm_colors)))

message(glue("sites: {nrow(sites)} across both conditions | ",
             "{sum(sites$condition == '10 mM')} at 10 mM, {sum(sites$condition == '1 mM')} at 1 mM"))
message("cm_class counts (NA here would add a stray legend key):")
print(table(sites$cm_class, useNA = "ifany"))
```

## Axis order

Genera are ordered by library size, largest at the top, so the input panel reads as a ranking and the other
three are read against it.

```{r axis}
lib_n <- tax %>% count(genus_display, name = "n_input")
small <- lib_n %>% filter(n_input < MIN_GENUS_N) %>% pull(genus_display)
collapse_axis <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% small, "Other", x)

tax    <- tax    %>% mutate(axis = collapse_axis(genus_display))
sites  <- sites  %>% mutate(axis = collapse_axis(genus_display))

axis_levels <- tax %>% count(axis) %>% arrange(n) %>% pull(axis)
tax   <- tax   %>% mutate(axis = factor(axis, levels = axis_levels))
sites <- sites %>% mutate(axis = factor(axis, levels = axis_levels))
message(glue("{length(axis_levels)} axis levels",
             if (length(small)) glue("; {length(small)} pooled into Other") else ""))
```

## Panel A — library input

```{r panel_a, fig.width=4, fig.height=7}
dA <- tax %>%
  group_by(axis) %>%
  summarise(accessions = n(), viruses = n_distinct(taxid), .groups = "drop")

# bars = accessions, dots = distinct viruses (TaxIDs). Mapped to a scale so they get a legend;
# without one the dots read as an unexplained annotation.
pA <- ggplot(dA, aes(y = axis)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = accessions, fill = "Accessions (sequence records)"), width = 0.72) +
  geom_point(aes(x = viruses, colour = "Viruses (distinct NCBI TaxIDs)"), size = 1.8) +
  geom_text(aes(x = accessions, label = accessions), hjust = -0.3, size = 2.6, colour = "grey25") +
  # No legend: panel A is too narrow for one, and a legend wider than its panel overflows
  # across the neighbours -- its background rectangle is the "translucent block". The two
  # series are named in the subtitle instead, which has the width for it.
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Accessions (sequence records)" = "#BFBFBF"),
                    name = NULL, guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Viruses (distinct NCBI TaxIDs)" = "#3A0CA3"),
                      name = NULL, guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22)), n.breaks = 4,
                     sec.axis = dup_axis(name = NULL)) +
  labs(x = "Accessions in the library", y = NULL,
       title = "A  Library input",
       subtitle = glue("grey bars = {comma(nrow(tax))} accessions; ",
                       "dots = {comma(n_distinct(tax$taxid))} viruses (TaxIDs)")) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.9, colour = "grey40"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.2),
        legend.position = "none",
        plot.margin = margin(2, 10, 1, 2))
pA
```

The dots matter here: **439 accessions are 273 viruses**, because segmented jingmenviruses contribute one
accession per segment. Where a bar is far to the right of its dot, that genus is segmented.

## Panel B — stall-positive accessions

```{r panel_b, fig.width=3.6, fig.height=7}
dB <- sites %>%
  group_by(axis, condition) %>%
  summarise(n_acc = n_distinct(plain_accession), .groups = "drop") %>%
  complete(axis, condition, fill = list(n_acc = 0)) %>%
  left_join(dA %>% select(axis, accessions), by = "axis") %>%
  mutate(pct = ifelse(accessions > 0, 100 * n_acc / accessions, NA_real_))

pB <- ggplot(dB, aes(x = n_acc, y = axis, fill = condition)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.72) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COND_COL, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18)), n.breaks = 4,
                     sec.axis = dup_axis(name = NULL)) +
  labs(x = "Accessions with >=1 site", y = NULL,
       title = "B  Stall-positive",
       subtitle = "gate: >=2 of 4 replicates") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.6, colour = "grey40"),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 10, 1, 2),
        legend.position = c(0.98, 0.02), legend.justification = c(1, 0),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.size = unit(0.7, "lines"),
        legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key = element_blank())
pB
```

## Panel C — sites by CM class

```{r panel_c, fig.width=4, fig.height=7}
# .drop = FALSE keeps factor levels with no rows. Without it a class that never occurs
# (class 3 and class 4 here) gets a legend key with nothing to draw -- an empty white box.
dC <- sites %>% count(axis, condition, cm_class, name = "n", .drop = FALSE)
message(glue("panel C: {nrow(dC)} rows; classes with zero sites: ",
             paste(setdiff(names(cm_colors), unique(as.character(sites$cm_class))),
                   collapse = ", ")))

pC <- ggplot(dC, aes(x = n, y = axis, fill = cm_class)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.72) +
  facet_wrap(~condition, nrow = 1) +
  # limits pins every class into the legend in a fixed order, so the two libraries' legends
  # match even where a class has no sites in this one
  # breaks + labels indexed by name, so a class with no sites still gets its own coloured key
  # and the labels cannot slide out of step with the colours
  scale_fill_manual(values = cm_colors,
                    breaks = names(cm_colors),
                    labels = unname(cm_labels[names(cm_colors)]),
                    name = "CM class", drop = FALSE, na.translate = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12)), n.breaks = 3) +
  labs(x = "Sites", y = NULL,
       title = "C  Sites by CM class",
       subtitle = "lowest E-value per site") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.6, colour = "grey40"),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        strip.background = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(size = 8),
        # a real gutter between the facets: without it the left panel's last label runs
        # straight into the right panel's "0" and reads as one number ("3000")
        panel.spacing.x = unit(1.1, "lines"),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 8, 1, 2),
        legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.7, "lines"))
pC
```

## Panel D — feature length

```{r panel_d, fig.width=3.2, fig.height=7}
# Same construction as viromelib's panel 4: boxes with outliers suppressed, the actual points
# jittered over them, coloured by region. A boxplot alone hides how few features some genera have.
dD <- sites %>% distinct(axis, accession, feat_len, region) %>% filter(!is.na(feat_len))
BAR_W <- 0.72
message(glue("panel D: {nrow(dD)} features | regions: ",
             paste(names(table(dD$region)), table(dD$region), sep = "=", collapse = ", ")))

pD <- ggplot(dD, aes(x = feat_len, y = axis, fill = region)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(colour = region), outlier.shape = NA,
               width = BAR_W * 0.42, linewidth = 0.25,
               position = position_dodge(width = BAR_W), show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = region), shape = 16, size = 0.35, alpha = 0.45,
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.height = 0.12, dodge.width = BAR_W),
             show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = region_colors, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = region_colors, name = NULL, drop = TRUE) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), breaks = c(0, 500, 1000, 1500),
                     labels = c("0", "500", "1,000", "1,500"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02)),
                     sec.axis = dup_axis(name = NULL)) +
  # override.aes must supply one value per legend KEY, and only the regions present get keys
  # (flaviLib has two of the three, no intergenic features), so nothing is hard-coded here.
  guides(fill = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, shape = NA)),
         colour = "none") +
  labs(x = "nt", y = NULL,
       title = "D  Feature length",
       subtitle = "features carrying >=1 site") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 7.6, colour = "grey40"),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 1, 2),
        legend.position = c(0.98, 0.04), legend.justification = c(1, 0),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6.8), legend.key.size = unit(0.7, "lines"),
        legend.background = element_blank(), legend.key = element_blank())
pD
```

fig

## Raw counts: genus x CM class

Unrounded counts, one table per Mg2+ condition, for pasting into a slide. Written as CSV and, if
`writexl` is installed, as XLSX — copying a block out of Excel keeps the grid when pasted into
PowerPoint, where a CSV opened as text does not.

Every CM class appears as a column even when it has no sites, so the two conditions (and the two
libraries) have identical columns and can be put side by side.

```{r raw_counts}
cm_levels <- names(cm_colors)

raw_counts <- function(cond_label) {
  base <- tibble(axis = levels(sites$axis)) %>%
    left_join(dA %>% select(axis, accessions, viruses) %>% mutate(axis = as.character(axis)),
              by = "axis")
  sc <- sites %>%
    filter(condition == cond_label) %>%
    mutate(axis = as.character(axis),
           cm_class = factor(as.character(cm_class), levels = cm_levels))
  wide <- sc %>%
    count(axis, cm_class, name = "n", .drop = FALSE) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = cm_class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
  for (lv in cm_levels) if (!lv %in% names(wide)) wide[[lv]] <- 0L
  wide <- wide[, c("axis", cm_levels)]
  names(wide) <- c("axis", unname(cm_labels[cm_levels]))
  acc <- sc %>% group_by(axis) %>%
    summarise(`Accessions with a site` = n_distinct(plain_accession),
              `Sites` = n(), .groups = "drop")
  base %>%
    left_join(acc, by = "axis") %>%
    left_join(wide, by = "axis") %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(.x, 0))) %>%
    rename(Genus = axis, `Accessions in library` = accessions, `Viruses (TaxIDs)` = viruses) %>%
    arrange(desc(`Accessions in library`))
}

tbl_10 <- raw_counts("10 mM")
tbl_01 <- raw_counts("1 mM")

write_csv(tbl_10, file.path(OUT_DIR, "raw_counts_genus_x_cm_10mM.csv"))
write_csv(tbl_01, file.path(OUT_DIR, "raw_counts_genus_x_cm_01mM.csv"))

# long form, both conditions, for anything that wants to re-pivot
bind_rows(tbl_10 %>% mutate(Condition = "10 mM"),
          tbl_01 %>% mutate(Condition = "1 mM")) %>%
  relocate(Condition) %>%
  write_csv(file.path(OUT_DIR, "raw_counts_genus_x_cm_both.csv"))

if (requireNamespace("writexl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  writexl::write_xlsx(list(`10 mM` = tbl_10, `1 mM` = tbl_01),
                      file.path(OUT_DIR, "raw_counts_genus_x_cm.xlsx"))
  message("-> raw_counts_genus_x_cm.xlsx (two sheets)")
} else {
  message("writexl not installed; CSV only. install.packages('writexl') for the XLSX")
}

# totals, as a check that nothing was lost in the pivot
message(glue("10 mM: {sum(tbl_10$Sites)} sites across the table vs ",
             "{sum(sites$condition == '10 mM')} in the data"))
message(glue("1 mM:  {sum(tbl_01$Sites)} sites across the table vs ",
             "{sum(sites$condition == '1 mM')} in the data"))
```

```{r raw_counts_10, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tbl_10, caption = "flaviLib 10 mM Mg2+ — raw counts by genus and CM class")
```

```{r raw_counts_01, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(tbl_01, caption = "flaviLib 1 mM Mg2+ — raw counts by genus and CM class")
```

A row's `Sites` is the sum of its CM-class columns, and `Accessions with a site` is at most
`Accessions in library`. The two messages above check the first of those against the data, so a
pivot that silently dropped a level would show up as a mismatch rather than as a quietly short table.

## Caption draft

```{r caption, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat(glue("
**flaviLib input and output by genus.** The axis is NCBI genus where one is assigned
({sum(!is.na(tax$genus))} of {nrow(tax)} accessions); where it is not, the lowest assigned taxonomic group
is used and marked '(unranked)', and accessions with neither are grouped as '(unclassified)'. Family is not
used as the axis because the library spans only three families.
(**A**) Accessions in the ordered library per genus (bars) and distinct viruses, i.e. NCBI TaxIDs (dots);
the two differ because segmented genomes contribute one accession per segment
({comma(nrow(tax))} accessions, {comma(n_distinct(tax$taxid))} viruses).
(**B**) Accessions with at least one stall site passing every gate in >=2 of 4 replicates, for each Mg2+
condition. The two conditions were peak-called separately and are not pooled anywhere in this figure.
(**C**) Stall sites coloured by the covariance model with the lowest cmsearch E-value at that site.
(**D**) Length of the features carrying at least one site.
"))
```
